subject: Map kickoff: evaluation success metrics & closure plan
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam@connecthealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation kickoff: defining success & exit gates

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. ConnectHealth is ready to move into an 8-week evaluation but we need a concrete MAP that captures success criteria, exit gates, and acceptance tests so we can sign off internally. High level asks:
- A short list of objective success metrics (performance, fidelity, cost targets)
- Clear pass/fail exit gates and how they map to rollback or extension decisions
- Concrete acceptance tests we can run/endorse (load, regression, data handling)
- A proposed timeline with milestones and who at Redwood / ConnectHealth owns each item

Attached is our one-page scope (evaluation-scope.pdf) — it includes some sample traffic profiles and a preliminary list of redlines from Prod Ops.

Can you send a MAP draft by early next week? Also please confirm any compliance evidence you need while the eval runs (SOC2 items, access logs).

Best,
Sam Ortega
Director, Product Integrations
ConnectHealth

Attachments: evaluation-scope.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-16T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff: defining success & exit gates

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the scope doc.

Attached is a first-pass MAP draft (redwood-map-draft.xlsx) — summary below. I kept it intentionally concise so your legal, security, and ops partners can scan fast.

1) Objectives (what success looks like)
- Integrate Redwood inference for document summarization across 3 clinical workflows
- Maintain user-facing latency and throughput targets while keeping unit cost within budget

2) Core success metrics (pass = green)
- Latency: median < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for 2k token context under typical load
- Throughput: sustain 10 RPS steady-state with <5% error rate
- Quality: rouge-like concordance > 0.82 on provided evaluation set (sample attached)
- Cost: average token-cost per call <= $0.006 (target)

3) Exit gates (immediate stop / escalate)
- Security/data-handling violation confirmed (unredacted PHI in logs)
- Failure to meet critical SLOs for 3 consecutive business days during test window
- Reproducible model hallucination in >5% of safety-critical prompts

4) Acceptance tests (concrete, executable)
- Smoke (day 0): basic end-to-end inference against your sample documents (5 examples)
- Regression (week 2): run Redwood regression harness against baseline model outputs (script attached)
- Load (week 4): 10 RPS soak for 2 hours with synthetic traffic matching your profile
- Cost validation (week 6): run long-tail traffic mix and measure token cost reporting vs. target
- Compliance check (continuous): audit logs exported daily; access control review on week 1

5) Timeline & owners (8-week plan)
- Week 0: Kickoff, credentials, data exchange (Owner: ConnectHealth / Sam)
- Week 1: Smoke + access control check (Owner: Redwood / Monica)
- Week 2: Regression tests, initial quality assessment (Owner: Redwood / Marcus)
- Week 4: Load soak + latency tuning (Owner: Redwood infra)
- Week 6: Cost validation + business review (Owner: Redwood / Laura)
- Week 8: Final acceptance review & close decision (Joint)

Notes: a) We recommend a canary model variant (quantized v1) for steady-state to limit cost while a non-quantized model is used during regression checks. b) Please confirm a procurement contact and any vendor onboarding paperwork timelines.

If this looks good I can update the spreadsheet with exact test scripts and a checklist we can tick off as we go.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett | Head, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Adding technical acceptance criteria and a short test plan from infra/serving side. Quoting Laura below for context.

On Mon, Jun 16, 2025 at 10:15 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> 4) Acceptance tests (concrete, executable)
> - Smoke (day 0): basic end-to-end inference against your sample documents (5 examples)
> - Regression (week 2): run Redwood regression harness against baseline model outputs (script attached)

Technical additions:
- Model / runtime variants: run the regression against both: a) baseline fp16 model b) 4-bit quantized variant. Pass condition: concordance delta <= 2% between variants for the evaluation set.
- KV-cache correctness: for multistep summarization flows, ensure context stitching matches reference outputs (script will assert token-level diffs)
- Perf thresholds for scale: under the 10 RPS soak, p95 must not grow >30% from baseline single-node numbers. If it does, infra will capture traces and automatically scale.
- Observability: we will push a temporary Grafana dashboard (link in Drive) for your SREs. Alert thresholds: p95 > 500ms OR error rate > 3% -> pager to ConnectHealth on-call.
- Rollback plan: if a critical SLO is breached for more than 2 hours during the load window, we will automatically switch traffic to a lower-cost fallback model and initiate a postmortem within 48 hours.

I attached the minimal test harness we use (test-scripts.sh) — it's a bash wrapper that runs the regression harness and uploads a simple report to the shared Drive.

Happy to walk through the scripts on a quick call.

— Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
